symptom: `mxcli check -p` reports E009 "This position requires Boolean, but the expression has kind Decimal" on `hoursBetween(…) : 4 < $Max` (Evora ConversationalUI.TokenMonitorSettings_GetGranularity / TraceFiltering_GetGranularity, 7 conditions). Studio Pro and mxbuild accept them; `mxcli check` without -p passes, so only project-backed checks show it.
cause: Neither of the two obvious suspects (wrong `:` precedence, or wrong typing of a comparison over a division). The MDL grammar already had `:` in multiplicativeExpression; the separate expression checker's hand-written lexer (mdl/exprcheck/lexer.go) did not know the character and emitted a TokError. parseMul saw no operator, parseCmp saw no comparison, and Parse deliberately skips E014 for a trailing TokError — so the tree was just `hoursBetween(…)` (measured: shape `hoursBetween(...)` before, `(< (: hoursBetween(...) 4) Max)` after), a Decimal, in a Boolean slot.
file: mdl/exprcheck/lexer.go (TokColon), parser.go (parseMul, inferKind), infer.go, unknown_funcs.go, recovery.go
fix: Lex `:` as TokColon; parseMul takes it at the one left-associative multiplicative level with `*`, `div`, `mod`; every switch that names "div" (inferKind → Decimal, SourceIsArithmeticDecimal, the unknown-funcs decimal test) also names ":"; TokColon is a recovery boundary.
insight: An error token that the top level is told to tolerate is a silent truncation: everything after it is never parsed, so any rule that types the whole expression is typing a prefix. When a checker exempts a token kind from the trailing-token error to avoid false positives, the false positive moves to the type rules instead of going away. Two parsers for one language (ANTLR grammar + exprcheck) drift independently — the grammar had `:` all along. Test: TestColonDivision_* asserts the parse tree as an S-expression rather than a kind, since a kind can be right for the wrong tree; reverting the fix fails all three. Evora describe → `check -p` clean and re-exec reports `2 documents already in sync`, .mpr sha unchanged.
